summary.text: Stratospheric aerosols are long-lived sulfate particles that form when sulfur dioxide from an eruption rises into the stratosphere and reacts with water vapor.
They reflect sunlight and cool the planet for a time, and after a large eruption they can stay aloft for a year or more.
Because this cooling happens naturally after eruptions, some have proposed deliberately injecting aerosols into the stratosphere to reduce global warming.

facts.label: Main ingredient
facts.value: Sulfate formed from volcanic sulfur dioxide

facts.label: Time aloft
facts.value: A year or more after a large eruption

facts.label: Pinatubo, 1991
facts.value: Cooled the globe about 0.5 °C for up to three years

facts.label: Early proposal
facts.value: Mikhail Budyko suggested sulfate aerosols in 1974

items.prompt: A volcano throws out a huge ash cloud along with sulfur dioxide gas. Which part ends up cooling the planet for a year or more?

options.label: The ash, which hangs in the air for decades
The sulfur gas, which forms high sulfate particles
The heat of the lava, which escapes to space
The steam, which falls back as snow worldwide

items.explain: Ash falls out fairly quickly, but sulfur dioxide rises into the stratosphere and forms long-lived sulfate particles that reflect sunlight.

items.prompt: After Mount Pinatubo erupted in 1991, roughly how much did global temperatures drop?

options.label: About 5 °C
About 0.05 °C
About 10 °C
About 0.5 °C

items.explain: The 1991 Pinatubo eruption cooled global temperatures by about 0.5 degrees Celsius for up to three years.

items.prompt: Why does a layer of sulfate particles high in the sky make the ground below cooler?

options.label: It bounces some sunlight back before it arrives
It traps heat close to the ground at night
It soaks up carbon dioxide from the air
It speeds up winds that carry heat away

items.explain: Sulfate aerosols reflect sunlight, which cools the planet; this raises albedo and dims incoming light.

items.prompt: One proposal to slow global warming takes its idea straight from what big eruptions do. What would it involve?

options.label: Pumping carbon dioxide into old volcanoes
Painting city roofs and roads white
Putting reflective particles high in the stratosphere
Planting forests on fresh lava fields

items.explain: Stratospheric aerosol injection would add aerosols to the stratosphere to create the dimming and higher albedo that volcanic winters cause naturally.

items.prompt: If people did try to spread aerosols in the stratosphere on purpose, what is the leading idea for getting them up there?

options.label: Setting off small volcanic eruptions
Firing them from cannons on mountaintops
Spraying them from ships at sea level
Flying them up in custom-built aircraft

items.explain: Custom aircraft are the leading proposed method of delivery.

items.prompt: Two eruptions release equal amounts of sulfur dioxide. In one the gas reaches the stratosphere; in the other it does not. Which cools the planet for longer?

options.label: The one whose gas reached the stratosphere
The one whose gas stayed lower down
Both cool for the same length of time
Neither, since sulfur gas warms the planet

items.explain: In the stratosphere the gas forms long-lived sulfate aerosols that reflect sunlight and can stay aloft for a year or more.
